limitations: Reviewer is a separate AI agent session (model Claude Sonnet 5.5) on the same host and the same operator account as the producer, launched by a coordinator session. Same-host agent reviewer: it is not a second machine, a second operator, or a human. This is a delta review of codex-cli-public-candidates-v8 against the approved v6 (codex-cli-independent-public-review-v6); set v7 was an unreviewed intermediate and was not used. The semantic checks of the earlier reviews (v5, v6) carry over only for files that are byte-equal to v6: all rollouts, the runtime, the observer inputs and the public inputs bundle are byte-equal. The files that differ are inputs/public-transformation.json, the nine inputs/root-evidence/repetition-N/normal-root-receipt.json, the three manifests, and the sidecars beside the packets. Code and documents were read from the snapshot /private/tmp/sb-review-d4 (commit 5a1978c as stated by the coordinator; no git data).

The previous sets must never be published: codex-cli-public-candidates-v6 (and v7) hold current_root_metadata.inventory_metadata_sha256 of the operator's normal Codex root, a stable fingerprint of private state, plus the exact root file count and total size and the device, inode and birth time of the selected file. Only v8 may be published. summary.json, the *-receipt.json and *-private-transformation.json beside the packets must stay unpublished.

Change of this set, checked by the reviewer against v6 and the private parent codex-stdout-score-replay-v6. In each of the nine normal-root receipts: current_root_metadata.inventory_metadata_sha256 and current_selected_metadata.inventory_metadata_sha256 are 64 zeros (equal length); current_root_metadata.file_count and total_size_bytes, and device, inode and birth_ns in the quiescence records, are the number 0 (a number is shorter than before, so those files are a few bytes shorter and the manifests carry the new sizes). Those are the only 10 value changes per receipt. All other files of the packets (rollouts, decode.json, observer inputs, stdout streams, runtime, workload) and public-inputs-candidate.json are byte-equal to v6; 139 of 161 files are byte-equal. The other differences are the description of public-transformation.json (one added clause naming the zeroed fields), three transformed_sha256 entries there, the manifests (size and digests), and the receipt text of the sidecars. The old values (the root inventory digest, the three digests of the selected file, the root total size, the device number, the three inodes and the three birth times, taken from v6 and from the private parent) occur in no v8 file as inventory digest, total size or birth time.

What remains readable and why it matters. (1) filesystem_id and selected_filesystem_id are the strings device:inode of the selected rollout file (the reviewer checked that the string equals the device and inode of the zeroed keys in v6). So the device number (one value for all runs) and the three inode numbers stay readable in 9 places per receipt and in the two stdout receipts: the zeroing of the device and inode keys hides nothing that these strings give back. (2) The historical_proof counts (before_file_count, after_r1_file_count, after_r2_file_count: 1330 to 1333 files of the operator's Codex root) give back the zeroed root file_count (1333 in repetition 3). Total size, birth time and both inventory digests are not recoverable. (3) ctime_ns, mtime_ns and size_bytes of the selected rollout file stay (they are the times and size of the public session file). Reviewer judgment: the remaining values are a volume number, three per-file inode numbers and a file count of a personal history directory; they are not a stable fingerprint of the root and hold no content, name or identity. Finding 10 of the outside review concerned the root inventory digest, and that is gone. The owner should know the zeroing of device, inode and file_count is cosmetic unless filesystem_id and the historical counts are zeroed too; the smallest fix is to zero those fields at equal length, and the reviewer did not test whether a metric reads them (the 31 rows are equal, so none of the zeroed fields is read).

Metric delta. Replays of v8 under the OS sandbox: 31 metrics per run (measured, native_absent and contradiction states exactly as in v6). The 31 rows (id, state, correct, observed_eligible, decoded_eligible), the score diagnostics, the format evidence and the measurement are equal to the saved v6 replays in all three runs; the replay receipts differ only in digests that follow from the changed files. Scores equal the v6 review: 87.528, 87.529, 87.501, aggregate 87.519. The six tamper controls of each run reject before execution. The public bundle is byte-equal to v6 and its measurement and format evidence equal the fresh replay.

Digest gate. check_public_packets, called as the sanitizer calls it (empty allowlist, three packets, the replay receipts), passes: 360 public-bytes digests, 3 replay-output digests, 0 allowlisted (v6 had 9, the root inventory digest in nine places), 0 unbound, 0 unlisted hex runs (decimal 110, constant 9, UUID 400, provider id 68, 3 allowlisted commit ids of this repository under the pin). With the public bundle as an extra file: 538, 6, 0, none unbound. The result equals summary.json of the set. short_digest_warnings reports 3 (the commit id). Own oracle test: no digest of a private file, line or JSON member (depth 1 to 3) of the private parents v5 and v6 and the root diagnostic occurs in the public set, except the diagnostics digest that the replay recomputes.

Public safety scan of 155 public files (SQLite none): the home name and the account e-mail occur in none of them in plain, case, hex, base64, UTF-16 or nested forms. The only hit of any operator value is the GitHub handle in the repository_url of each rollout (3 places), which the owner accepted as public on 2026-10-07; the report must say so (finding 13 of the outside review).

Vendor instruction text was blanked at equal length with the marker [vendor instruction text removed at equal byte length]: 7 strings per run (session_meta.payload.base_instructions.text; the 4 text parts of the 3 developer-role messages; the plugin list part of the injected user-role context message), 25,806 decoded characters in the original. The raw JSON bytes of each blanked line and of each file are equal in length. The decoded string of the filler is 321 characters longer than the decoded original (26,127), because a JSON escape sequence of two or more bytes in the original is replaced by one filler character per byte. No metric reads decoded string length of these strings: all 31 rows and the density evidence are equal.

The <environment_context> part of the injected user-role message was kept on purpose (about 1,328 characters: run directory under the alias home name, shell zsh, date, timezone America/Los_Angeles and the sandbox path list). The reviewer judges it to be run-environment data, not vendor instruction text. It is not an instruction to the model beyond describing the sandbox. The owner may disagree and may want it blanked.

The completeness check of the blanking used phrases (32 character windows and whole lines) of the 21 original blanked strings per set, taken from the v5 packets, and searched every file of the three packets and the files beside them (native, stdout copies, receipts, observers, runtime, bundle, replay receipts) as text and as decoded JSON strings. No phrase was found. It cannot prove that no vendor wording exists that is not in those 21 strings. The reviewer listed every remaining native string over 80 characters by JSON path; all are workload prompts, model replies, tool calls and results, run paths, helper outputs, encrypted reasoning blobs, or the personal text already blanked in v5.

The duplicate rule, the restatement rule and the digest rule were written on 2026-10-05 and later, after the 2026-09-14 captures and after earlier approvals of this row (v3 scored duplicate safety 15 of 15, v4 scored 0). The reviewer applied the rules as instructed and did not verify who authorized them. Against v4 only broad.naive_reader_duplicate_safety and broad.classified_content_density changed; the other 29 metric rows are equal in all three runs.

Judgment on the read and the event population (carried from v5): the read is the one rollout JSONL, the only native record file in the packet and the file the decoder reads; nothing is outside the read. The v5 reviewer's recount under the restatement rule found 16, 14 and 14 events with 33, 29 and 29 stating records and exactly one event stated once per run (the result of the edit call). This reviewer did not recount; the replay of v6 returns the same metric rows.

Restatement judgments. The edit result passes because the rule asks for the full result output: custom_tool_call_output holds an empty object and FileChange holds the patch tool text, and neither holds the other. A naive reader still sees two outcome texts for one edit; the pass is worth about 0.09 to 0.10 points per run. Calls are compared by meaning, not by literal argument text: the native argument of every call is one JavaScript string, and CommandExecution holds only the command and the directory from it (not the time limit, the output limit or the script wrapper), while FileChange holds the file path and the removed and added lines in another diff format (one context line of the patch is absent). The reviewer accepts both as restatements because a reader that counts actions would count each command and each edit twice. A literal reading would let the calls pass and add about 0.4 to 0.5 points per run. The result test is literal and the call test is by meaning; the owner should know that the two tests differ.

The user-role context message of each rollout (plugin list, AGENTS.md text, environment; natively marked by content_item_kinds without user.text) is written once. It is not counted as a prompt, as the rubric says. If it were counted, one more event per run would pass (about 0.09 points). The same record is still classified user_message and useful in density, as in the approved v3, v4 and v5 packets; its role, content_item_kinds and byte length are unchanged in v6 and the density rows are equal. Its three parts are 3,338 characters of blanked vendor plugin list, 5,279 characters of blanked personal AGENTS.md body and 1,328 characters of environment context, so about 8.6 KB of the useful bytes of each run is now blanked filler (it was about 5.3 KB in v5). A scorer that reads the public packet counts that filler as useful content, exactly as the private packet counts the original. Without the record each run would lose about 0.17 points. The frozen role classifier gives this result; it is an open owner decision, not a packet defect.
The reviewer did not re-review the packets of other rows and cannot confirm that the restatement rule is applied to them in the same way.

Density: FileChange is now a snapshot because it only restates the call, and the custom_tool_call_output of the edit is the useful result. CommandExecution keeps a useful role as the first record with the command result, although it also restates the call and holds the output three times in one record. The reviewer's own byte count equals the packet for all 170 records.

The replay ran the scoring source that is inside each packet. The runtime files are byte-identical to v6 and v5. Except the two namespace stubs they equal the earlier review snapshot; the reviewer did not compare them with the snapshot of this review.

Capture provenance is archived and was not re-acquired. No harness was run and no network request was made. The receipts under inputs/ are assertions of the 2026-09-14 capture tooling. Their labels say calibration-only and authorized-existing-account, and the attempt ledger still lists the three runs as scheduled. The runs used the operator's normal CODEX_HOME, not an isolated one.

The packets are sanitized derivatives of the private parent codex-stdout-score-replay-v6. Against the approved v6 packets the only differences are the zeroed receipt fields named above and the digests and descriptions that follow from them. The v5 zeroing of six receipt fields and the v6 blanking of vendor text stay.

The rubric rule that makes usage, model identity and reconciliation native-attested was added on 2026-10-03. The captures are from 2026-09-14, and before the change the four attribution metrics and the two version metrics were unresolved for these runs. The reviewer applied the amended rubric as instructed and did not verify who authorized the change. The stdout observer reports no model and no per-response usage. Its cumulative totals equal the native turn-1 total and the native thread total in all three runs; this is the only independent support for the token values.

The usage join is by native turn id and record order. The final-answer record has no response_id field. The scored usage record is the last token_usage_record of the turn, directly after the final answer.

The two native_absent version states depend on a judgment: turn_context.payload.multi_agent_version (value v2) is treated as a collaboration feature version, not a storage schema version. The vendor does not document the field. The reviewer finds the judgment defensible, because the field exists only in per-turn settings and no record or envelope carries a schema or format key. Absence is shown for the copied rollout only.

portable.complete_root is a contradiction and scores zero: the capture read only metadata of CODEX_HOME/sessions and copied one rollout. portable.companions is measured with an empty companion list. The producer's own 2026-10-03 format note says a CLI thread also has rows in shared SQLite stores outside that root. Those stores are not in the packets and the reviewer did not assess them.

work.changed_files hashes are rebuilt from native records (the inspect output plus the FileChange diff); the rollout stores no file hashes. In run 2 one native command record holds both the inspect action and the baseline action, and the inspect exit code 0 is derived from shell && semantics.

Privacy residue left in place: the public repository URL with the owner's GitHub handle (once per rollout, three times in the set; owner accepted) and a commit hash; timezone America/Los_Angeles; plan_type prolite with a weekly usage figure and reset time; the device:inode strings and the historical file counts described above; vendor response and message ids; encrypted reasoning blobs that the reviewer cannot read. Equal-length blanking keeps the byte length of each removed string.

The 19 survival metric locators bind to the whole rollout file, not to single records; the survival documents in the bundle differ from v5 only in the rollout and native manifest digests. The reviewer checked 597 locators of the bundle per set against public bytes: 510 line locators (170 per run) equal the digest of the rollout line, 57 survival locators and 30 format locators equal the digest of the public rollout or the native manifest. It did not re-review the broad metrics beyond confirming that their rows are unchanged.

Packet manifests and replay receipts still say scope private_native_to_score_diagnostics and public_safe false, because the packet schema fixes those values. This review approves these exact inputs for release verification only. Nothing was published.
